findings.text: Offers a completion deferral helper for block I/O that arranges task-context completion when the caller is in atomic context. It is idempotent with respect to an in-task marker and reports through its boolean result whether deferral was arranged.

Provides a uniform completion reporting path that associates a block layer status with a bio and then drives normal end of I/O handling. Convenience wrappers report a generic I/O failure and a retryable would-block condition without requiring callers to select status codes.
Estimates vector allocation needs for an iterator, requiring no additional vectors when the iterator already has bvec form and otherwise bounding the page count by a caller supplied segment limit.

Estimates bounce vector needs distinctly for writes and reads against a fixed maximum, reserving extra capacity for the read bounce buffer while treating bvec iterators like other iterators for sizing.
Write direction is encoded in the lowest bit of the operation flags word, so testing that bit distinguishes writes from other operations.
Initializes a bio to use storage immediately trailing the bio object for its inline vectors, with caller supplied device, vector capacity and operation flags.
Inline vectors are laid out contiguously after the bio header in memory, allowing a bio with embedded capacity to be addressed without separate allocation.
Bounds vector usage for appending a memory range, allowing multiple pages when the address lies in vmalloc space based on page offset and length, and otherwise limiting to a single vector.
Releases pages referenced by a bio only when the bio is marked as holding pinned pages, with an option to mark pages dirty on release; otherwise it has no effect.
The device identity associated with a bio is obtained from the disk object reachable through its block device pointer.
In the routed configuration, block cgroup association helpers for bios are inert placeholders, and the punt helper submits the bio directly on the current path rather than redirecting it.
Reassigns the target device of a bio while clearing remap state, dropping throttle state when the device actually changes, and refreshing cgroup association for the new device.
A bio list is a singly linked queue described by head and tail pointers, with an empty list represented by null head and a static initializer providing that empty state.

Queue operations preserve head and tail consistency across insertion at either end, concatenation in either order with optional reinitialization of the source, and peek, pop and bulk-take removal. Popped entries are detached, size is determined by traversal, and iteration follows next links from head.

A bio list alternates between empty with null head and tail and populated with linked entries, where initialization and bulk-take force empty, insertions and merges force populated, and single pop returns to empty only when removing the last entry.
Chained bios carry a chain marker and a remaining count that is incremented with ordering against prior flag update, supporting completion counting for split or chained I/O.
The minimum bio pool size is two entries.

A bio set combines a slab cache indicator with front and back padding, per-CPU allocation caches, dedicated pools for bios and vectors, rescue machinery comprising a workqueue, work item, queued list and its serializing spinlock, and a hot-unplug list node. Initialization state is reflected by presence of the slab.
A set is considered initialized when its slab pointer is present. A separate helper clears the polled operation marker from a bio operation word.
Zone-append detection is disabled without zoned-device support and otherwise recognizes either the zone-append operation or an emulation marker on the bio.

Bitfield helpers enforce at build time that masks are constant, non-zero and contiguous, that constant values fit within the selected field, and that the register type is wide enough for the mask, failing compilation otherwise.

Provides a family for extracting and inserting contiguous bitfields by mask, including maximum value query, fit testing, constant and runtime preparation and extraction, signed extraction with sign extension, and in-place modify of a pointed-to register with pointer checking.

Supports runtime masks through multiplier and mask derivation with overflow reporting, plus generated little-endian, big-endian and native helpers for encoding, replacing, pointer-replacing and decoding field values with endianness conversion.

Bit reversal resolves to architecture support when available and to generic helpers otherwise, selects compile-time evaluation for constant inputs, and treats four-byte reversal as byte-swapped word reversal.
Fibre Channel application identifier length is one hundred twenty nine.

Congestion reporting uses a fast atomic check with a slow-path fallback in one configuration and unconditionally reports uncongested with inert throttling in the other, where the cgroup state lookup for a bio yields null.
The root cgroup state constant is encoded as an error pointer for invalid argument.

Low-level inline-encryption operations comprise keyslot programming and eviction with idle guarantees, plus optional hardware-wrapped key handling for deriving a software secret from an ephemeral form, importing from raw, generating new, and preparing long-term form into ephemeral form, each with documented success and error returns.

An inline-encryption profile holds driver supplied capability descriptors for operations, maximum data-unit-number size, supported key types, per-mode data-unit-size support and optional power-managed device, alongside private slot count, slot lookup table and sizing, per-slot data, idle list with wait queue, and synchronization objects.

A read-write semaphore coordinates all low-level operation invocations and mutations of the slot hash, allowing concurrent read-mode slot lookups that exclude concurrent mutation, while a separate spinlock guards the idle slot list.
Encryption modes are numbered invalid zero, AES-256-XTS one, AES-128-CBC-ESSIV two, Adiantum three, SM4-XTS four, with five as the exclusive upper bound.
Raw software keys use bit value one and hardware-wrapped keys use bit value two.
Maximum raw key size is sixty four bytes, maximum hardware-wrapped key size is one hundred twenty eight bytes, with the overall maximum defined as the larger of the two.

Several helpers carry misuse hazards: list size walks the chain linearly, bitfield preparation and modification trap compilation on non-constant, zero, non-contiguous or oversized uses and on undersized registers, and multi-page vector allowance applies only to vmalloc addresses.
Block I/O completion and device assignment helpers serve as inline entry points for ending I/O with status, deferring completion to task context, and retargeting a bio to a device.
Routed headers define conventional include guards to ensure single inclusion.
External barrier dependency for ordering before atomic update.
External barrier dependency for ordering before atomic update in alternate configuration.
External atomic increment dependency for completion counting.
External atomic read dependency for congestion fast path.
External address classification dependency for vmalloc detection.
External page offset dependency for span calculation.
External iterator classification dependency for bvec detection.
